Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE Dil.C OPINION NO. 138 S. 2010 DIRECTOR ANANIAS M. VILLACORTA OIC-DILG Region X1 Davao City Dear Director Villacorta: This has reference to the Memorandum dated 21 September 2010 of Director Fernando M. Valdez seeking clarification on these issues, to wit: "I. When does the A ug•ust 24, 2010 decision of the Supreme Court become final? Is it already final since the reinstatement of November 18, '2008 decision also calls also (sic) for the reinstatement of the entry ot-judgment made on May L' I, "2009? e. Anent the additional two seats in the local legislative body of the local government of Mati, would the August '24, 2010 decision have the legal effect of barring the 9th and 10th ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Members fi•om further attending legislative sessions since the number of council seats is reverted back to eight (8)P Are they still entitled to salary and other monetary benefits attached to their positions? In reply thereto, please be informed that the SILG has already signed an Advisory dated 24 September 2010 and addressed to all concerned Regional Director and Field Officers regarding the status of the sixteen (16) cities recently reverted into municipalities by the Supreme Court. For your ready perusal, attached hereto is a certified photocopy of the aforesaid Advisory. Along this line, we beg to disagree with your position that the reinstatement of the 18 November 2008 Decision of the Supreme Court in its recent Resolution promulgated on 24 August 2010 has also the effect of reinstating the entry of judgment already made on the 18 November 2008 Decision. While drafting the aforesaid Advisory, the Central Office made verification with the Judgment Division of the Supreme Court on whether a Motion for Reconsideration was timely filed vis-å-vis the 24 August 2010 Resolution of the Supreme Court. The Judgment Division answered in the affirmative but such Motion for Reconsideration is still to be included in the High Court's agenda. Given this latest pleading filed with the Supreme Court, the Department is of the view that Section 2, Rule 36 of the Revised Rules of Court is still applicable, viz: "Sec. g. Entry of judgments and linal orders.— If-no appeal or motion for new trial or reconsideration is filed within the time provided in these Rules, the judgment or final order shah' förthwith

-2- be entered by the clerk in the book of entries of judgments. The date of finality of the judgment or final order shall be deemed to be the date of its entry. The record shall contain the dispositive part of the judgment or final order and shall be signed by the clerk, with a certificate that such judgment or final order has become final and executory. Based on the foregoing, a decision rendered by a court, tribunal or quasi- judicial agency does not attain finality pending the resolution of a motion for reconsideration or appeal of said decision filed. On a final note, please be informed that the Department has also already made the corresponding manifestation and/clarification on the matter from the Supreme Court, which is the ultimate arbiter of the contentious issues raised. Please be guided accordingly. Very truly yours, JESUS B. DOQUE IV Director III Ls/17
